facts.text: The Glico Man sign, installed in 1935, shows a giant athlete on a blue track and has become a symbol of Glico candy.
Matsudaira Tadaaki named the canal and avenue Dōtonbori, with “bori” from “hori” meaning canal, even though Nariyasu Dōton fought on the losing side.
Otakoya, a takoyaki stand that opened in 1972 near Tazaemonbashi, was moved in 2010 because the original site was municipal land.
Dōtonbori runs along the canal from Dōtonboribashi Bridge to Nipponbashi Bridge in Namba, famous for its neon‑lit streets at night.
By 1662 the area boasted six Kabuki theatres and five Bunraku theatres, underscoring its long‑standing theatrical heritage.
River cruises leave from the Tazaemonbashi Bridge Boat Dock, where guides offer local history in several languages.
